description: Add a learnable per-head scalar gain on q and k after the existing RMSNorm in attention (initialized to 1, set in init_weights, and trained in the scalar Adam group), so the attention logit scale is learned rather than fixed.

Replace the squared-ReLU MLP in every block with a SwiGLU MLP (SiLU-gated up-projection, hidden width round(2/3*4*n_embd), same ~8*n_embd^2 parameter count), including initialization for the new gate projection.
Implement a batch-size ramp-up strategy starting at 2^17 and linearly increasing to 2^19 over the first 40% of training time.
Switch to grouped-query attention by setting the number of KV heads to half the query heads (num_heads // 2, so 2 KV heads shared across 4 query heads at the current DEPTH=8 / model_dim=512 config).
Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 to extend the linear decay period of the learning rate.
Add a Z-loss regularization term based on logits to stabilize logit norms and reduce late training drift.
Change each transformer Block to a parallel form, x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), with one shared pre-norm feeding both branches.

issues: Bug: the cosine warmdown runs backwards. p = (1 - progress) / WARMDOWN_RATIO equals 1 when warmdown starts and 0 when it ends. 0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)) is therefore 0 at the start and 1 at the end. At the start of warmdown the LR multiplier drops from 1.0 straight to FINAL_LR_FRAC. It then climbs back to 1.0 by the end of training, so the model finishes at peak LR. The intended form is 0.5*(1 - cos(pi*p)), or the same expression with cos(pi*(1-p)).

This bug fully explains the large regression (1.1763 vs 1.1145, Δ = +0.0618). The run tests a broken schedule (a sudden drop, then a rise back to peak LR), not a cosine warmdown. It must not be taken as evidence that cosine warmdown is worse than linear.
No integrity problems: the diff only touches the LR schedule function. Evaluation, data, seed lines and the prepare import are unchanged.

z cannot be recomputed exactly because the incumbent standard deviation is not given. The reported z = -10.944 implies std ≈ 0.0618 / 10.944 ≈ 0.00565, which is plausible. The sign is consistent with the candidate being worse, and the reject decision stands.
Recommendation: veto this as a meaningless test of the hypothesis. Fix the sign and rerun if cosine warmdown is still worth a slot.

description: Replace the linear learning rate warmdown with a cosine decay during the final fraction of the training budget.
Apply the successful decoupled weight decay modification to the AdamW step in train.py.
Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 to prevent the learning rate from decaying to zero during the warmdown phase.

Weight each target token's cross-entropy by its UTF-8 byte length (precomputed per vocab id from the tokenizer's decoded strings, falling back to weight 1 if decoding fails) so the training loss tracks the bits-per-byte objective.
Keep the token-embedding and lm_head Adam learning rates constant during the warmdown period while applying the multiplier only to Muon and scalar parameters.

Maintain an EMA of the model parameters, updated after each optimizer step with a warmup-capped decay (min(0.999, (1+step)/(10+step))), and copy the EMA weights into the model just before the existing final evaluation, leaving the optimizer's training weights untouched.
Reduce Newton-Schulz iterations in the Muon optimizer from 5 to 3 to allow more training steps within the time budget.

Adds a zero-initialized token-embedding table whose lookup, scaled by a per-layer scalar initialized to 0.5, is added to the value projection in the second half of the blocks, with the table trained at EMBEDDING_LR and the scalars in the resid Adam group.

issues: Integrity is fine: the diff only changes Block.forward to put an RMSNorm on the attention and MLP branch outputs before they are added to the residual stream. It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, data loading, seed lines, the prepare.py import or the evaluation call.

No bug makes the result meaningless. This is a legitimate architecture change. One modelling caveat: norm() has no learnable gain, so each block now adds a fixed unit-RMS update and cannot learn how much each branch contributes. Also, if c_proj is zero-initialised, the norm of a near-zero branch output gives very large gradients early in training. Either could explain the worse score, but neither is an integrity problem.

The numbers agree with the decision. The candidate scored 1.1385 against an incumbent mean of 1.1145 over 16 runs, so it is 0.024 worse (higher bpb). A z of -4.249 under the convention (incumbent − candidate)/sd points the right way and supports reject. There are no claims in the submission that conflict with these numbers.

z cannot be recomputed because the incumbent's standard deviation is not given. Back-solving from the reported z, the sd implied is about 0.0056 if z = diff/sd, or about 0.0055 if z = diff/(sd·sqrt(1+1/16)). Either seems plausible for run-to-run noise.
There is only one candidate run, but at z ≈ -4.2 a replicate would almost certainly not change the reject, so it is not worth spending a slot.

description: Adds a parameter-free RMSNorm on each sublayer output (attention and MLP) before it is added to the residual stream, keeping the existing pre-norms and residual scalars unchanged.

Tie lm_head to the token embedding (shared weight, std 0.02 init), drop the separate UNEMBEDDING_LR group, and raise DEPTH from 8 to 9; note that ASPECT_RATIO rounding makes model_dim jump from 512 to 640, so the parameter count and wall-clock will grow rather than stay constant.
Replace the aggressive Newton-Schulz coefficients in MuonAdamW with a smoother, more conservative set to reduce sensitivity to late-training gradient scale.

Sequence-length curriculum: train at half sequence length (1024, batch doubled to 128) for the first 30% of the time budget, then switch to full 2048-length batches, keeping tokens per optimizer step at TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE so grad_accum_steps is unchanged.
Replicate slot 9's successful change by set-wise setting the Adam betas for embedding/lm_head groups to (0.9, 0.95) instead of using the shared ADAM_BETAS.
